o: Explain how a character set maps characters to numerical codes.
Explain pixels, resolution and colour depth in uncompressed bitmap images.
Calculate bitmap size in bits, bytes and decimal MB.
c: Character sets map symbols to numerical codes stored in binary. The booklet's ASCII sequence uses C = 01000011, D = 01000100, E = 01000101, F = 01000110. Unicode covers far more scripts and symbols.
A bitmap stores the colour of each pixel in a grid. Resolution is width in pixels × height in pixels.
Colour depth is the number of bits per pixel. More bits allow more possible colours.
Revision booklet calculation chain: width × height = pixels; × colour depth = bits; ÷8 = bytes; ÷1000 = kB and ÷1000 again = MB (decimal units; ignore metadata/headers unless specified).

mastery.task: A school image must be below 1 kB (decimal), with no compression. Choose the larger possible image: 40 × 20 at 8-bit depth, or 20 × 20 at 16-bit depth. Show working and justify.
mastery.hint: Calculate both sizes in bytes first, then compare with 1000 bytes.
mastery.answer: 40×20×8/8 = 800 bytes; 20×20×16/8 = 800 bytes. Both occupy the same 800 bytes, so neither is larger; both meet the under-1 kB limit. Their resolution/colour trade-offs differ.
